description: C and TypeScript strict transaction immediate HTTP denials after staging
qualification: normal local combined-source Linux node, ephemeral demo trust, actual JetStream provider and controlled loopback listener
observations: Each real component was built from its captured controlled variant, demo-signed and admitted by the local node with actual event-provider requirements and no immediate HTTP grant.

Each variant stages a state write and event intent before attempting HTTP, and returns its declared rejection only after receiving the typed permission-denied result. Both durable results were rejected, fresh queries found the key absent, and namespace inspection found no pending effects or encoded state.

The controlled listener observed no connection, the broker held zero messages, and node and broker owners retired cleanly. The initial C variant fell through to the scan handler and aborted; the corrected variant was rebuilt and rerun.
limitations: This covers one controlled denial per guest, not all authority, cancellation, crash, fuel or memory cases. It does not count guest executions.
The node contains unmerged local combined source; production trust, hosted CI and installed distribution are not established.
